speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with postpartum fever and abdominal tenderness; please tell me how many days ago you gave birth and what the highest temperature you have reached is. Additionally, have you experienced any changes in your vaginal discharge, such as a foul odor or increased amount?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum endometritis with associated urinary tract infection.

The prolonged labor, uterine tenderness, fever, and foul-smelling discharge are classic signs of endometritis. Given the increased urinary frequency, I suspect a concurrent urinary tract infection. The decrease in bowel sounds may indicate ileus, a common complication. I will need to see your complete blood count and urinalysis results to confirm these findings. REQUEST TEST: CBC and Urinalysis.
